title: English Opening: Anglo-Indian Defense
line: Black brings the knight out first, and White takes the whole center with pawns.

steps.text: Black brings the knight out first and keeps its choices open.
Bring your knight out. It watches the center squares d5 and e4.
Push the king pawn two squares. With the pawn on c4 and the knight on c3, White takes the center.

also.g1f3: That is sound too, and calmer. This lesson takes the center.
also.d2d4: That leads to the Queen's Gambit or an Indian defense. This lesson takes the center another way.

steps.text: Push the pawn on and chase the knight on f6.
steps.after: Black strikes back at your knight.

steps.text: Take the knight. Black takes one of yours too.
Take back with the pawn on b2. It moves toward the center.
Push the pawn in front of your queen two squares. Pawns on c3, c4 and d4 give White more of the center.
steps.after: Material is level. White has more of the center, Black has quick development.

summary: When Black waits with a knight, White can take the center with pawns and chase the knight.
